{"predictors": [
  {"name": "Inventory Turnover", "construction": "Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) divided by Average Inventory for the fiscal year", "rationale": "Firms with higher inventory turnover may be more efficient in managing their resources, which could lead to higher profitability and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Dividend Surprise", "construction": "Actual dividends paid compared to analyst consensus estimates, computed quarterly", "rationale": "Firms that pay higher dividends than expected may be more profitable or financially healthy than anticipated, leading to positive price reactions.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Earnings Announcement Drift", "construction": "Cumulative abnormal return from two days after quarterly earnings announcement to the next earnings announcement", "rationale": "If markets are slow to incorporate earnings news, there might be a drift in stock prices following the announcement.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Tax Rate", "construction": "Total Taxes Paid divided by Pre-Tax Income for the fiscal year", "rationale": "Firms with lower tax rates might have more net income and cash available for growth or dividends, leading to higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Capital Expenditure Growth", "construction": "Year-over-year percentage change in capital expenditures", "rationale": "Firms that are investing heavily in their business might be expected to grow faster, leading to higher stock returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "CEO Age", "construction": "Age of the CEO at the end of the fiscal year", "rationale": "Older CEOs might be more conservative in their business approach, which might lead to lower volatility and higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Productivity", "construction": "Revenue divided by the number of employees at the end of the fiscal year", "rationale": "Firms with higher productivity may be more efficient, leading to higher profitability and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Geographic Diversification", "construction": "Number of countries in which the firm operates at the end of the fiscal year", "rationale": "Firms operating in more countries might have more diversified revenue streams, reducing risk and potentially leading to higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Customer Concentration", "construction": "Percentage of revenue that comes from the firm's largest customer", "rationale": "Firms that rely heavily on a single customer might have more business risk, which could be reflected in their stock returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"},
  {"name": "Litigation Risk", "construction": "Number of ongoing lawsuits against the firm at the end of the fiscal year", "rationale": "Firms with more litigation risk might have more uncertainty about their future cash flows, which could lead to lower stock returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}
]}
